title: spec review: S2 v6: Dispatch provider="claude" executor rows through run_worker with the row's model, capacity-aware
spec:
Respec of T-1348: depends_on moved to S1 v6 T-1352 and acceptance ids rewritten to the gate-parseable tests/x.py::test_name form (acceptance.py:8 does not read Class::test). Spec otherwise unchanged. Goal T-1334. After S1, pick_executor can return a provider="claude" row, but executor.start (executor.py:487) sends every non-codex pick to _exhausted() (fallback tier by complexity), and the daemon's dispatch capacity (capacity.snapshot / eligible_executors_from_snapshot, capacity.py:54, used at daemon.py:806) treats every row like a Codex row. Plug and play means a Claude row runs as itself within Claude capacity. 1. orchestrator/executor.py start(): when ex.provider == "claude": acct = pool.pick("execute") (re-checked here: S1 eligibility reserves nothing); None -> bus.update status held, hold_reason "no account with headroom", return {"status": "held"}. Else bus.update(task, executor=ex.id, tier=ex.id); ex.roll_day(); ex.day_tasks += 1; pool.save(); run spawn.run_worker(task_id, account_id=acct.id) in a background thread registered in _fallback_threads exactly like _exhausted() (executor.py:535-569); handed_off=True so the dispatch reservation passes to run_worker. Return {"status": "dispatched", "executor": ex.id, "provider": "claude"}. No fallback/review_rule fields. ex None keeps _exhausted(). Unknown provider -> held, hold_reason "unknown executor provider

". 2. orchestrator/spawn.py run_worker: model (spawn.py:1538) = the row model when pool.executor_identity(t["tier"]) is provider "claude" with a model, else cfg["models"][t["tier"]] as today. Execute branch (spawn.py:1564): executor = row id for a row-routed task, legacy f"claude:{tier}" otherwise; the "Claude fallback executor (Codex is unavailable)" line only for legacy, row-routed gets "You are the routed executor". executed_by (spawn.py:1657) uses t["executor"]. Claim stays "claude:" (spawn.py:1603). 3. orchestrator/capacity.py: snapshot rows carry provider; in eligible_executors_from_snapshot a claude row additionally needs snapshot["claude_workers_free"] > 0 and at least one account with headroom in snapshot["accounts"] (use fields the snapshot already has). Codex rows unchanged. 4. orchestrator/daemon.py _codex_available (daemon.py:454, drives fallback mode): a claude row counts only when not cooling and pool.pick("execute") returns an account. 5. Fix rounds: executor.resume_plan returns fresh for non-codex parents (executor.py:279); keep it, test it. 6. README.md "Executors and routing" (README.md:278): provider="claude" rows (id, full model id, quota_group, roles, complexity band), Claude headroom from [[claude_accounts]], reviewer never runs the executing model, plug-and-play recipe: add a row to add a model; enabled=false on every codex row to run without Codex. Test behaviour per acceptance id: test_start_runs_claude_row_with_its_model (only a claude row eligible -> run_worker called with account_id, executor and tier = row id, _exhausted not called); test_claude_row_holds_without_headroom (every account cooling -> held, 'no account with headroom'); test_fix_round_for_claude_row_is_fresh (resume_plan -> mode fresh); test_run_worker_uses_row_model (claude --model = row model, executor = row id; legacy tier 'sonnet' still via [models]); test_claude_row_needs_claude_capacity (snapshot excludes a claude row when claude_workers_free is 0 or no account has headroom; codex rows unchanged). Define each as a method in a unittest.TestCase. No .orchestrator/pool.toml edit (Planner adds the opus55 row after merge). No new dependencies. Additive; git revert restores Codex-only dispatch. 8 files: one behaviour, not split.

resume_hint.raw: y daemon tick, so check it is side-effect-free (capacity.snapshot is deliberately read-only). Prefer the snapshot account fields. The spec also does not cover running_claude_workers (daemon.py:~470). It counts by 'claude:' prefixes on assigned_to or executor. Row-routed tasks use executor=row id, so counting relies on assigned_to='claude:<acct>' from the claim. Between dispatch and claim the inflight_claude_dispatches reservation must cover them.","severity":"low","line":455}]],"suggested_spec_changes":["Decide how the claude branch of start() interacts with pool.reserve and the daily budget. Either call pool.reserve(task_id, ex.id, 'execute', t) and return status 'budget' with the same hold_note handling as the codex path, or state that run_worker owns the reservation and add a test. Check daily_budget_tasks before dispatching.","Make admit() count claude rows against one shared free['claude'] pool, taken from claude_workers_free and bounded by the number of accounts with headroom, and decrement it on each admission. Add a test where two tasks compete for one free Claude slot.","Say how snapshot['fallback'] and daemon._codex_available treat provider='claude' rows, and use one shared definition. Add a test for the mixed case where all codex rows are cooling and a claude row is healthy.","Audit every reader of t['tier'] (daemon.py:1101 and 1275, cli.py:590, scorecard.py:193, attribution, review routing) and either list the needed changes and tests in scope or stop writing tier=ex.id.","Set handed_off=True only after thread.start() succeeds. Specify what happens if run_worker raises (task status, day_tasks). Have run_worker reject an unknown or disabled row id with a hold reason instead of falling back to cfg['models'].","Add acceptance tests for: two claude tasks admitted in one pass, a raising worker, the positive eligibility case, _codex_available with a claude row, and joining the background thread deterministically in test_start_runs_claude_row_with_its_model."]}
